title: Dollar holds steady as Middle East tensions simmer, oil rises

excerpts.text: Oct 21 (Reuters) - The dollar held steady against most major currencies on Wednesday as investors weighed developments ​in the Middle East conflict, which has revived demand for the US currency as a safe haven amid concerns about oil-driven ‌inflation.

The euro slipped 0.1% to $1.122 and is now down almost 1% this month. Traders remained cautious on the single currency as France grapples with widespread anti-government protests and a worsening fiscal outlook that has pushed its 10-year borrowing costs to 24-year highs.

Sterling inched 0.1% up to $1.338. Data showed UK inflation rose more than expected last month, strengthening the case for a Bank of England ​rate increase in November and adding pressure on the government to support households in next week's budget.
The dollar index , which measures ​the US currency against six peers, was little changed at 101.7 after declining almost 0.3% on Tuesday and touching 101.50, its lowest since October 1.
